reviews.findings: Independent source-grounded follow-up audit confirms Exclude/Not_relevant_topic under the two-dimensional screening rule. The paper evaluates LLM trust reasoning and explicit prompting for fictional PhD mentorship, with secondary computational/symbolic trust discussion; it does not investigate social work, structural bias, gender effects, diversity, feminism or algorithmic fairness. All three existing positive-category evidence terms match the original Paper text. The earlier wrong year is corrected for all three aliases by the now validated local metadata projection (2025-06-11; preprint; arXiv); official arXiv v1 identity, title and four authors match. This accepts the screening classification, not all empirical claims or general deployment validity.
reviews.review_scope: Full main-text source-grounded audit of identity, all ten categories and decision derivation; no new blinded PRISM run or human verification. Structured analysis fields are not required for Exclude. Main text read locally and checked against official arXiv HTML; OCR-corrupted table cells were not used to infer numerical findings.

AI_Literacies.reason: Model reasoning ability is evaluated, not human AI-literacy acquisition; the fictional research discussion does not establish a literacy study.

Generative_KI.reason: Four LLMs are the evaluated systems in two trust-reasoning and role-playing case studies.

Prompting.reason: Trust-theory system prompts, user dialogue prompts and role instructions are the operational research method in Sections3-4.

KI_Sonstige.reason: Computational/symbolic multi-agent trust models motivate the problem; Section5 proposes future symbolic-AI integration. A secondary explicit strand, without a separate implemented classical-model experiment.

Soziale_Arbeit.reason: Generic fictional PhD mentorship; no social-work practice, professional social-work education or target population examined.

Bias_Ungleichheit.reason: Hallucinations, trust and misjudgments are reported, without analysis of structural discrimination or group inequality.

Gender.reason: Gendered names and roles in fictional scenarios are not analysed as gender effects.

Diversitaet.reason: Inclusive environment is dialogue/generated-response content; no paper-level diversity or representation contribution.

Feministisch.reason: No feminist method or structural gender-power analysis.

Fairness.reason: No algorithmic fairness criteria, metric or fair-system intervention; trust/safety/ethics vocabulary alone is insufficient.
